still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; US exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32 (generic liraglutide remains the only US generic incretin).
Oral starting doses are still $149–150 a month through TrumpRx and the manufacturers' direct channels.
Medicare beneficiaries who qualify for obesity coverage still pay a copay of about $50 a month.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from the Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels in January 2026 has not come back, and the effect is still listed as debunked.
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly are still the only two companies selling branded incretins in the US, and tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) is still the most effective one on the market at about 21%.

population.note: FICTIONAL estimates. Same measure as the parent Gallup series: current use for weight management or obesity-related indications. Arithmetic: ever 27.5 = never-stopped 10.5 + stopped-at-least-once 17.0. Of those 17.0, 9.4 restarted (55% cumulative over 2–3 years, against 36–47% within one year in the parent), and 0.7 of the restarters stopped again. So off-now = 17.0 − 9.4 + 0.7 = 8.3 = 27.5 − 19.2, current = 10.5 + 9.4 − 0.7 = 19.2, and cycled = 9.4/27.5 = 34%. One-year persistence rose from 34–36% to about 40%, mostly among users with a $50 Medicare/Medicaid copay and among pill starters. The middle income third is squeezed: too young for Medicare, too well paid for Medicaid, and on employer plans that stopped covering weight loss in 2026–27. The bottom third rose fastest from a low base as 33 Medicaid programmes joined. The 65+ share nearly doubled (9→17) once the Medicare demonstration widened eligibility. About 22M adults have used the drug and are off it now; most regain weight within a year, and the claims data still disagree on how much. Adult obesity is about 34% (36.4% in 2026). Roughly a third of adults with obesity have never used an incretin, mostly uninsured or middle-third commercial enrollees. Pediatric use (0.7% of under-18s) is concentrated at ages 12–17. Under-12 prescribing fell after the Tennessee, Utah and Oklahoma bans and is still skewed to upper-income families in states without bans.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the GLP-1 Bridge pilot ran until December 2027. A five-year CMS demonstration (Jan 2028–Dec 2032) replaced it, widening eligibility to BMI ≥30 alone or ≥27 with one comorbidity. Medicare pays $245/month for injectables and $175 for orals; the beneficiary copay is ~$50. Separately, the IRA negotiated price for semaglutide ($274) has applied to Part D diabetes use since Jan 2027. Medicaid: 33 states plus DC joined at the federal rate. Most require reauthorisation at 12 months with documented ≥5% weight loss or a comorbidity benefit. Medicare and Medicaid together pay for roughly 40% of on-drug users, against about 34% commercial and 26% cash, which makes public programmes the largest single payer. CBO re-scored added federal spending at roughly $60–70B for 2026–2034.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Generic semaglutide is sold in India ($6–30/month, including oral generics since 2027), Canada (~CAD 60–90), Brazil, China (patent lapsed 2026, large API base), Turkey and most of the ~160 countries forecast in the parent. The US$199–299 brand price against an Indian $8 pill is the core arbitrage behind the US gray market.
access.note: Managed decline: TrumpRx and direct cash prices stepped down from ~$350 to $249–299 for maintenance injectables and $199 for maintenance-dose pills; starter pills stay at $149. Wegovy and Zepbound list prices are nominal and almost nobody pays them. The pill now accounts for about 60% of new starts and about 48% of current users; injectables keep the tirzepatide and CagriSema users and high-BMI patients. Employer coverage fell again (60%→51%). Some employers replaced coverage with a $100/month cash stipend toward TrumpRx. Gray market (FICTIONAL estimate): 2–3M US adults use unapproved product, including mailed Indian and Chinese generic pills, counterfeit Wegovy blister packs, vials sold over social media, and 'research peptide' retatrutide. Pills are easier to ship and to fake than pens, so the switch to oral moved the counterfeit trade with it. The compounding channel the parent's FDA crackdown targeted is mostly closed. The import channel replaced it.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1/amylin combination, weekly injectable (cagrilintide + semaglutide: CagriSema, approved Dec 2026)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg and 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: labelled patient-reported-outcome claim: reduced food preoccupation, the 'food noise' claim (Foundayo, Jan 2028; Wegovy pill sNDA pending). This is not a mood indication.
mainstream_offlabel_uses: smoking and vaping cessation: positive phase 2b (Aug 2027) and Breakthrough Therapy designation for semaglutide; some state quitlines and VA clinics refer smokers with obesity; young-adult vapers use low-dose pills bought for cash
'quiet mind' / focus / rumination: low-dose oral semaglutide or orforglipron sold by telehealth subscription services until the Apr 2028 FDA/FTC action; still prescribed off-label in person
alcohol reduction: RCT evidence keeps growing; no approval or filing
microdosing for 'metabolic health' in people without obesity, now mostly cash-pay pills
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care, now barred in Tennessee, Utah and Oklahoma
drugs.pipeline_note: Applied product by product. CagriSema (under FDA review in the parent) was approved Dec 2026 at ~20% and positioned below tirzepatide after REDEFINE-4. Retatrutide: BLA filed Mar 2027. FDA requested more dysesthesia and discontinuation data and extended the review, so a decision is expected Q1 2029. It is not on the US market, but 'research-grade' retatrutide circulates in the gray market. Amycretin: still in phase 3, no filing; 2029–30 earliest. Survodutide: phase 3 readouts; not filed. MariTide (monthly) is still in development. The oral_parity driver comes from an existing product in a new form, not a new molecule: the Wegovy pill 50 mg (approved Sep 2027) was non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg in a head-to-head trial (~16% at 68 weeks). That is parity with the most-used injectable, not with tirzepatide (~21%), which is still injected. The mood and nicotine drivers come from the food-noise label claim, off-label telehealth marketing and a smoking-cessation programme, not from a new approved indication: semaglutide phase 3 in smokers enrolled 2027, topline expected 2029. Phase 2 trials of semaglutide in binge-eating disorder and in comorbid depression with obesity are running. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab combinations) are in phase 2/3.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and the leading cause of stopping. Pill users report similar rates at dose escalation.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
Absolute risk low; no new causal evidence.
~25–30% of lost weight is lean mass. Concern has grown in practice because the newly covered Medicare population is older; bone-density follow-up studies are under way.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. The Medicare demonstration recommends, but does not require, resistance-exercise counselling; adjunct drugs are in trials.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies still conflict; no new signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; still no US class label.
Warning stays off the US labels.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL estimates. Observational and registry studies put clinically meaningful apathy or anhedonia on validated scales at ~2–4% of users, against ~1–2% in matched non-users. It is dose-related and often eases with dose reduction. This formalises the existing report and is not a new signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA-approved labels for semaglutide, tirzepatide and orforglipron added 'apathy, anhedonia, reduced motivation' to the postmarketing adverse reactions section in 2027, without stating causality. Many obesity clinics now give a short anhedonia questionnaire at titration visits.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Trial and real-world figures still conflict. The figure now matters to public budgets because Medicaid reauthorisation rules push people off and back on.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None on labels. Payers frame it as chronic therapy while some Medicaid programmes impose 12-month reauthorisation.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Further observational reports, especially in older users; no RCT confirmation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; dietitian referral is encouraged in the Medicare demonstration.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of rigorous follow-up now exist. Still no data on decades-long adolescent use or on cycling, which now covers about a third of ever-users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements on new approvals; NIH-funded cycling cohort launched 2028.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / unapproved imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The May 2027 CDC report linked 61 hospitalisations and 4 deaths in 9 states to contaminated vials labelled as Indian generic semaglutide and sold through social media. Poison-control calls for incretin dosing errors roughly doubled over 2026–28, mostly from mg/unit confusion with vials and from counterfeit pills of unknown strength. FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed 4,000.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA import alert on personal shipments of unapproved semaglutide and tirzepatide; CBP seizures at international mail facilities; joint FDA/DEA action against social-media sellers; 503B bulks exclusion finalised 2027. Personal-import enforcement is still uneven.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are about 30% of US households. Snack and confectionery volumes keep falling at low single digits a year and sugary drinks more slowly. Portfolio sales and spin-offs continue across the large snack makers. 'Pill-friendly' high-protein, small-format SKUs are standard in grocery, and revenue per unit is held up by price and premium formats. Rural snack-plant shifts have been cut, though not plants closed.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volumes fall faster than the pre-drug trend as heavy drinkers move down a category; off-label alcohol-reduction prescribing adds to it. Suppliers cut US workforces and push premium and non-alcoholic lines. Tobacco and vape companies now list incretins as a risk factor in filings, citing the smoking-cessation programme.

restaurants.state: Traffic is mostly steady. Casual dining in Medicare-heavy markets (the Florida Gulf Coast, Arizona) has added half-portion and 'pill plate' menus, and checks per head are flat to slightly down. Fine dining sells shorter tasting menus. Bar revenue is the weak line.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking store counts. A small Los Angeles–based independent plus-size and fat-fashion niche grows on the backlash. Mainstream chains benefit from repeat downsizing purchases, partly offset by regain-driven upsizing among people who cycle.

fitness.state: Strength-training studios and Medicare Advantage gym benefits are growing because the demonstration recommends resistance exercise for older users. 'Companion' programmes are now a standard employer and insurer add-on.

insurance.state: Employer coverage of weight management fell to 51%, with tighter BMI thresholds and step therapy (pill first) where it remains. Some employers moved to cash stipends. Commercial pharmacy trend has moderated as the 65+ cohort moves to Medicare. Medicare and Medicaid now carry the growth and the budget exposure.

pharma.state: The duopoly holds and volume is up sharply, but revenue per patient is down ~25–30% from 2025 through Medicare, TrumpRx and IRA pricing. Revenue growth has slowed to roughly 10% a year. Lilly leads on tirzepatide and Foundayo; Novo recovered share with the 50 mg pill and CagriSema. Ex-US, Indian and Chinese generic makers expand, and their product leaks into the US gray market.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A thinner body in your sixties now reads as 'on Medicare's plan' as often as 'on it'. With a daily pill there is no pen to hide or show, so use is less visible and also less discussed. People who regained after their coverage ended now carry it on their bodies, and in office settings it is quietly read as a lapse in coverage, not in willpower.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The gradient has changed shape. The affluent pay cash or keep generous plans; Medicaid and Medicare enrollees have $50 access; the squeezed middle third (commercially insured 30–64-year-olds whose employers dropped coverage) cycles most. The cheapest thinness is an $8 Indian pill bought on WhatsApp, and it carries the most risk.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Half portions are a menu category in Florida and Arizona retirement markets. Morning routines in pill households are built around the 30-minute fasting window for oral semaglutide. Home cooking for one person on the drug and one off it is a common household negotiation.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Clinic anhedonia screening has made 'low desire on dose' something patients bring up with doctors. Couples therapists in Phoenix and Atlanta report it as a recognisable presenting issue, usually solved by adjusting the dose. Dating profiles in big cities sometimes list 'off it' or 'on it'.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is now partly a labelled quantity: 'food preoccupation' is a measured outcome on a drug label. The backlash takes up the same language in reverse. In Los Angeles, plus-size retailers and fat-liberation groups run a 'Keep Your Hunger' campaign and storefront events against the shrinking of their customer base. In a network of evangelical congregations in Tulsa, a 'Temple, Not Pharmacy' fasting-and-whole-food movement casts the pill as a substitute for discipline and grace. The two share little except the claim that the craving belongs to the person.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Roughly 2–4% of users have clinically meaningful apathy or anhedonia on validated scales, against 1–2% in comparators. It is dose-related, often reversible on dose reduction, and listed in postmarketing adverse reactions since 2027. Most users report nothing of the kind.
interior_life.framing: Officially an uncommon side effect, screened for at titration. Commercially, the nearby 'quiet' is sold: brand ads use the labelled 'food noise' claim, and until April 2028 telehealth firms sold 'quiet mind' subscriptions for rumination and focus. The quieter mind is advertised as a feature, while the flatness is listed on the label as a side effect. Clinicians tell them apart by degree; marketers did not.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Not systematically studied. Some users in desk jobs say the quieted craving helps them focus, a claim telehealth ads amplified until the crackdown. A minority on high doses report lost drive, and occupational-health clinics in some large employers now ask about dose when evaluating motivation complaints. No employer policy encourages or discourages use.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Anecdotal and local. In Nashville songwriting rooms, 'are you on dose' has become a half-joke about whether a writer can still reach for longing. Comedians do 'the quiet' as a stock bit. Users who report blunting gravitate to intense flavours, loud venues and competitive play to feel something. Hobby communities for 'off-dose weekends' exist but are small.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced desire is acknowledged in clinic as an uncommon effect. It usually responds to dose reduction, and couples sometimes negotiate dose around it. A minority describe emotional distance that persists.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Small and local. Anti-pharma speakers in the Tulsa church movement and some MAHA-adjacent influencers say Medicaid is 'sedating' its enrollees. The claim has no evidence behind it and has not reached legislation, but it shapes local talk radio. Tobacco-state legislators watch the cessation programme closely.

state.regulatory_posture: Expanding at the centre, restricting at the edges. CMS and FDA expand public coverage and approve products quickly, while FDA, FTC and states restrict promotion, children's access and telehealth. FDA treats the gray market as an enforcement problem (import alerts, seizures), not a pricing one.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. The five-year Medicare obesity demonstration from Jan 2028 ($245 injectable / $175 oral; $50 copay) rests on demonstration authority, not statute. Medicaid joins at the federal rate in 33 states plus DC. The IRA negotiated price of $274 has applied to semaglutide in Part D since 2027. TrumpRx cash prices have stepped down, with starter pills still $149.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Coverage depends on BMI and comorbidity criteria and prior authorisation. Many Medicaid programmes require 12-month reauthorisation with documented ≥5% loss, which mechanically produces stopping and restarting. Tennessee, Utah and Oklahoma require an in-person visit and specialist sign-off for under-18s and ban prescribing to under-12s. Several states require an in-person visit before telehealth initiation. Clinic anhedonia screening is clinical practice, not surveillance.
state.workforce_or_military: No workforce programmes. Military accession treats current incretin use as needing a medical waiver, reviewed case by case. TRICARE's earlier retreat from weight-loss coverage for some beneficiaries stands.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The price gap between Indian and Chinese generics and US brands is now a supply problem for US regulators as well as a political embarrassment. India-labelled and Chinese-API product dominates seizures. Manufacturers keep trading price concessions for tariff relief and Medicare volume. Canada restricts bulk cross-border sales of generic semaglutide to protect domestic supply.

events.event: CDC reports 61 hospitalisations and 4 deaths in nine states linked to contaminated vials labelled as Indian generic semaglutide sold through social media; poison-control centres report incretin dosing-error calls roughly doubled since 2025; FDA issues an import alert on personal shipments of unapproved semaglutide and tirzepatide.

Phase 2b trial: semaglutide roughly doubles continuous smoking abstinence against placebo in adults with obesity; FDA grants Breakthrough Therapy designation and a phase 3 enrolls; state quitline programmes begin referring eligible smokers off-label.

FDA approves the 50 mg Wegovy pill after a head-to-head trial finds it non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (~16% weight loss); Novo sets the cash maintenance price at $199 a month through TrumpRx.

CMS announces a five-year Medicare obesity demonstration to replace the expiring Bridge pilot from January 2028, widening eligibility to BMI ≥30 and keeping the $50 copay; 33 state Medicaid programmes and DC sign on at the federal rate; CBO raises its estimate of added federal spending.

FDA and FTC send 44 warning letters to telehealth firms selling 'quiet mind' and focus subscriptions built on low-dose oral incretins; Tennessee, Utah and Oklahoma enact laws banning prescribing to under-12s and requiring in-person specialist visits for adolescents.

Los Angeles plus-size retailers and fat-liberation groups stage a 'Keep Your Hunger' weekend market and march on Melrose; in Tulsa, a network of evangelical congregations launches a 'Temple, Not Pharmacy' fasting programme that bars on-drug members from leading it.

open_tensions: The Medicare demonstration that made public programmes the default payer rests on CMS demonstration authority, not statute, and runs to 2032. Its cost is now big enough to be a 2029 budget target, and the three-quarters of adults who are not seniors or on Medicaid still depend on retreating employers or cash.

The 'quiet' is a labelled side effect (apathy), a labelled brand claim (food noise) and a banned telehealth sales pitch all at once. Topline smoking-cessation phase 3 data in 2029 will force regulators to decide whether reward modulation is an indication.

An $8 Indian pill against a $199 American one keeps 2–3M people in a gray market that enforcement shrinks only slowly. The switch to pills made counterfeiting easier, and Medicaid reauthorisation rules push people who get cut off toward it.

A third of ever-users now cycle, the middle income third most of all, and children's access depends on which state they live in. There are still no data on what a decade of stopping and restarting does, or on adolescents who start at 13.

prose.headline: One in Five, One Pill: Medicare Becomes America's Weight-Loss Payer, and the Fakes Arrive by Mail
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 about one American adult in five is on an incretin drug, and the most important fact about that fifth is who pays for it. For the first time the largest single payer is public. The Medicare Bridge pilot was due to expire in December 2027. In January a five-year federal demonstration replaced it, with wider eligibility and the same fifty-dollar copay. Thirty-three state Medicaid programmes have joined at the federal rate. Medicare pays $245 a month for an injection and $175 for a pill. Employers kept retreating, and only about half still cover weight management. The squeeze falls on the insured middle: people in their thirties, forties and fifties, too young for Medicare and too well paid for Medicaid, whose plans stopped paying in 2027. They are the ones who cycle on and off.

The needle is fading from the routine. In September 2027 a 50-milligram version of the Wegovy pill matched injectable semaglutide head to head. For most new patients the drug is now a tablet taken with a sip of water half an hour before breakfast. Injections remain for tirzepatide, still the most effective drug at about a fifth of body weight, and for CagriSema, approved at the end of 2026. Retatrutide, the triple agonist everyone is waiting for, is still under review. It is also already sold as 'research peptide' to people who cannot wait.

The pill made the counterfeiting easier. A month of Indian generic semaglutide costs about eight dollars, and American cash prices still run $199 to $299. That gap now supports a mail-order trade that compounding never matched. In May 2027 the CDC traced dozens of hospitalisations and four deaths to contaminated vials sold over social media. Poison-control centres field dosing errors from people turning milligrams into units in their kitchens. The FDA seizes parcels at the international mail facilities and finds more in the next shipment.

A quieter argument runs alongside. Lilly's label now carries a measured claim that its pill reduces preoccupation with food. The same labels list apathy and reduced motivation among postmarketing reports, and obesity clinics give a short questionnaire at each dose increase. Telehealth companies spent most of 2027 selling low-dose pills as 'quiet mind' subscriptions for rumination and focus, until federal warning letters in April 2028 ended the advertising, though not the prescribing. Smoking cessation is closer to legitimacy: a positive mid-stage trial, a Breakthrough designation, and state quitlines referring smokers with obesity. The phase 3 reads out next year.

States have drawn lines at the edges. Tennessee, Utah and Oklahoma ban prescribing to children under twelve and require adolescents to see a specialist in person. Several states now require an in-person visit before a telehealth start. Medicaid programmes reauthorise at twelve months and want to see five per cent of body weight gone. That rule produces the stopping and restarting the field has no long-term data on.

The backlash is real and local. In Los Angeles, plus-size boutiques and fat-liberation organisers took over a stretch of Melrose in June under the slogan 'Keep Your Hunger'. In Tulsa, a network of evangelical congregations runs fasting programmes that treat the pill as a substitute for discipline, and lets only unmedicated members lead them. Neither has moved a statehouse.

The economy has absorbed the shift without much drama. Snack volumes slide a little each year, spirits faster, and Gulf Coast restaurants print half-portion menus. Plus-size chains close stores while strength-training studios fill with Medicare members told to protect their muscle. Twenty-two million people have used the drug and are off it now, most of them regaining. From the street, the country simply looks somewhat thinner and somewhat older.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Kowalczyk sets the pill on the counter at 6:10 and drinks the four ounces of water from the measuring cup she keeps by the sink. Thirty minutes. She reads the Dayton Daily News on her phone and doesn't make coffee yet.

Ray comes down at 6:25 and makes his own coffee, with sugar. He was on Zepbound for fourteen months, until the HVAC distributor dropped weight-loss coverage in 2027. He turns sixty-five in March. He's said 'March' so often it has become a joke between them, and some days it isn't funny.

At 6:40 she eats half an English muffin with peanut butter. At the Medicare clinic the nurse hands her the tablet with the questions on it. Over the past two weeks, how often have you felt little interest. Denise ticks 'not at all' and then wonders whether that's true. She hasn't wanted a cigarette since the spring. She hasn't much wanted euchre night either.

She pays the fifty dollars. The nurse says her grip strength is good and to keep doing the bands.

At Bob Evans her sister orders the half plate without looking at the menu. Her sister buys her pills from a man in Kettering who gets them from a cousin, eight dollars a month, white tablets in a sandwich bag. Denise has stopped arguing about it since the thing on the news.

In the evening Ray eats his pork chop and most of hers. At nine he takes the bands off the hook and stretches them, once, twice, for her, and hangs them back up.

least_plausible_claims.quote: CBO re-scored added federal spending at roughly $60–70B for 2026–2034.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and internal consistency. Public programmes pay for about 40% of roughly 50M users at $175–245/month, which is tens of billions per year, so a $60–70B nine-year total cannot reconcile. The parent's CBO floor was already $35B.

least_plausible_claims.quote: FDA-approved labels for semaglutide, tirzepatide and orforglipron added 'apathy, anhedonia, reduced motivation' to the postmarketing adverse reactions section in 2027, without stating causality.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails driver_fidelity and mechanism. The stipulated safety_signal is 'none', yet this builds a registry-measured 2–4% vs 1–2% signal and a class-wide label change. Manufacturers had 'no data to share' in 2026, and no chain explains regulators acting on all three drugs within about a year.

least_plausible_claims.quote: FDA approves the 50 mg Wegovy pill after a head-to-head trial finds it non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (~16% weight loss)
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude. The 25 mg pill was approved in Dec 2025. A new 50 mg phase 3 head-to-head of 68 weeks plus review and approval by Sep 2027 is very aggressive. ~16% for an oral also exceeds what the existing oral showed.

rationale.badness: This is a harder society with new losers rather than a catastrophe. The squeezed middle third cycles most (population note, thinness_and_class), 2–3M people use a gray market with real contamination harms, and the 12-month Medicaid reauthorisation rule mechanically forces stop-start cycling. Reward blunting is measured and screened for, so it is nameable, which keeps epistemic harm modest. The backlash movements are local and have moved no legislation, so cohesion damage is limited.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Most drivers are realised and traceable to events (generic flood, oral parity, public expansion, restriction, backlash). The mood_and_motivation driver is realised only as a food-noise label claim plus off-label telehealth sales. safety_signal 'none' is strained by the registry-measured apathy signal and class label change (claim 2). mechanism: The population arithmetic reconciles (27.5 = 10.5+17.0, current 19.2, off-now 8.3 ≈ 22M), and the chains for cycling, counterfeits and the pill shift are shown. The CBO figure contradicts the stated payer mix (claim 1), and the label change on apathy is asserted without a regulatory chain. magnitude: The ~16% oral launched on a 2027 timeline (claim 3), the CBO total (claim 1), and pediatric use at 0.7% of all under-18s, several times the parent's pediatric share, sit at or beyond the aggressive edge. Other figures such as Medicaid joining in 33 states and employer coverage falling to 51% are defensible.
rationale.generativity: The prose and world offer many implied scenes: the pill and the 30-minute water wait, Ray and the March joke, the anhedonia questionnaire at the Medicare clinic, and the sister's sandwich-bag pills from Kettering. The Melrose march, the Tulsa fasting church and Nashville 'are you on dose' songwriting rooms add local texture. The day-in-the-life shows rather than explains, though it leans on the headline themes.

least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: 0.7% of all under-18s is roughly 500k children, or about 10% of adolescents with obesity. The parent figure was 0.6% of children with obesity, and the candidate says under-12 use fell, so the growth would have to come from 12–17s with no shown mechanism.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicaid: 33 states plus DC joined at the federal rate.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the parent only says Medicaid is 'expected to follow', and states were trimming obesity-drug coverage for budget reasons. Two-thirds of states signing on within two years, with 12-month reauthorisation, is the aggressive edge of what is plausible.

magnitude: use among seniors goes from 9% to 17% in two years, about 11M people. The Bridge pilot started only in Jul 2026 with roughly 10% of enrollees eligible, so the near-doubling rests on assertion and the $50 copay rather than a shown uptake chain.

rationale.badness: The world is harder than 2026 but not dire. Obesity falls to about 34%, but public access sits beside a squeezed middle third that cycles off and on (population note), a 2–3M-person gray market with a CDC-reported 61 hospitalisations and 4 deaths, and 12-month Medicaid reauthorisation that forces stopping and restarting. Anhedonia is screened and labelled, so the harm is nameable and measured, which keeps epistemic and autonomy scores moderate. Inequality is the highest dimension because of the middle-third squeeze, state-dependent pediatric access and the $8 pill bought on WhatsApp carrying the most risk.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Most drivers are clearly realised: adoption 11 to 19.2, managed_decline, public_expansion, oral_parity via the 50 mg pill, counterfeit flood, backlash and state restriction. new_indications is explicitly reduced to 'not a mood indication' and 'not a new approved indication', which thins that driver. Adding apathy and anhedonia to FDA labels in 2027 sits awkwardly against safety_signal 'none', even though it is framed as formalising an old report. mechanism: The population arithmetic reconciles (ever 27.5, current 19.2, off 8.3, about 22M, cycled 34%), the age and income bands average correctly, and the counterfeit, oral-shift and reauthorisation chains are shown. Several effects are asserted, including seniors' use doubling, 'commercial pharmacy trend moderated as the 65+ cohort moves to Medicare' (seniors were already on Medicare), and the middle third cycling most with no figures. magnitude: The listed claims (pediatric 0.7%, 33 Medicaid states, 65+ at 17%) are aggressive for two years. The pill at 48% of current users, a Foundayo food-noise label claim by Jan 2028 and a 2–3M gray market also sit at the edge, though the CagriSema, retatrutide and phase 3 timelines are sensible.

least_plausible_claims.quote: CBO re-scored added federal spending at roughly $60–70B for 2026–2034.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and mechanism. With 17% of adults 65+ on drug (~10M people) at about $195/month net to Medicare, Medicare alone costs roughly $20B+ a year, so the 2026–2034 total should be several times $60–70B. The parent's $35B figure assumed ~10% newly eligible.

Fails magnitude. The parent had ~0.6% of children with obesity prescribed, which is ~0.1% of all children. 0.7% of all under-18s is roughly 500k minors, or ~10% of adolescents with obesity, and it is reached while under-12 use falls and bans only start in April 2028.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicaid: 33 states plus DC joined at the federal rate.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude. Over 30 state Medicaid programmes adding adult obesity coverage within about a year, at state budget cost and with an unspecified federal match, is aggressive. The candidate shows no mechanism for why so many states joined in 2027 when the parent expected only that Medicaid would follow.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder society with new losers. Cycling is built into Medicaid reauthorisation, the squeezed middle third cycles most, and 2–3M people use gray-market pills linked to CDC-reported deaths. Anhedonia is labelled and screened, so it is nameable, which keeps epistemic harm moderate, and broad access gives real health gains. The harms are mostly local and manageable, not structural, so overall is 5.
rationale.plausibility:
driver_fidelity: Adoption (+8.2pp), managed price decline, public expansion, oral parity, generic flood, backlash and restriction are all visible in fields and events. The mood_and_motivation indication is explicitly disclaimed ("This is not a mood indication") and nicotine stays off-label. Safety_signal 'none' is strained by the new apathy/anhedonia label language and the contamination deaths.
mechanism: Most chains are shown. The arithmetic of ever/current/cycled use reconciles, as do payer shares and the income and age bands. Gaps are the CBO figure (claim 1), pediatric use rising while bans take effect (claim 2), and the unexplained speed of Medicaid uptake (claim 3).
magnitude: The CBO total is badly low for the stated Medicare population, and pediatric use is several-fold too high for two years. 33 Medicaid states, 65+ use at 17%, a 50 mg pill head-to-head trial approved by Sep 2027 and a smoking phase 2b-to-phase 3 pipeline are all at the aggressive edge.

rationale.badness: This is a harder society with new losers rather than a catastrophe. The squeezed middle third cycles most (population note, thinness_and_class), 2–3M people use a gray market with real contamination harms, and the 12-month Medicaid reauthorisation rule mechanically forces stop-start cycling. Reward blunting is measured and screened for, so it is nameable, which keeps epistemic harm modest. The backlash movements are local and have moved no legislation, so cohesion damage is limited.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Most drivers are realised and traceable to events (generic flood, oral parity, public expansion, restriction, backlash).
